speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) to date, how many appeals have been received by the CPF Board for inclusion into the Silver Support Scheme; and (b) how many of such appeals have been acceded to.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Silver Support is the latest addition to our seniors' support schemes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Over the years, the Government has put in place a comprehensive framework to support seniors in their various needs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The first tier offers universal coverage for all seniors, for example, with MediShield Life for healthcare, Senior Citizen Concession Card for public transport and foreign domestic worker levy concessions for daily care at home.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The second tier provides another layer of support to a majority of seniors, for example, with Goods and Services Tax Voucher Scheme for utilities and healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And to supplement retirement incomes, we also have the Silver Housing Bonus and enhanced Lease Buyback Scheme for seniors to monetise their property.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The third tier is for a minority of seniors only, for those who need even more support.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, ComCare for short- and long-term financial assistance, Community Health Assist Scheme Blue, MediFund and Page: 26 MediShield Life Additional Premium Support for healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The Silver Support Scheme is the latest addition to the third tier of support.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, it is only meant for the minority of seniors.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It is targeted mainly at the bottom 20% of elderly Singaporeans aged 65 and above, with a smaller degree of support extended to up to the next 10% of seniors.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Specifically, we identify them as seniors who not only have little or no family support currently in their retirement years, but also did not manage to save enough for their retirement because they earned low wages over their prime working years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The eligibility criteria for Silver Support were announced by the Finance Minister at Budget 2016.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The first criterion is total Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions made during prime working years until the age of 55.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Wages were generally low in the early years of Singapore's economic development.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, a vast majority of our workers earned low wages during their younger days.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Among these two-third seniors, some owned smaller homes with less scope to monetise their assets and some currently continue to have lesser family support and lower household income.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: By combining the three criteria of total CPF contributions capped at $70,000, home ownership of 4-room Housing and Development Board flat or smaller, or living in 5-room flat or smaller, and lastly, household monthly income per person of not more than $1,100, we ensure that Silver Support goes to those seniors who need more help than the others.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: To help our seniors better understand the new scheme, we have set up a Silver Support website for them to check their eligibility and get clarifications on frequently asked questions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Seniors can also call the Silver Support hotline or visit any of the CPF Service Centres.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: To date, CPF Board has handled more than 28,000 enquiries.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We also disseminate information and distribute brochures on Silver Support through the grassroots network such as the Community Centres.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Pioneer Generation Ambassadors are also trained to explain the scheme to seniors during their house visits.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Among the cases processed, some have been rejected because these seniors have far exceeded the thresholds of the three criteria.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Some cases have been approved because the seniors' circumstances have changed in the last 15 months and they now meet all the three criteria.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There were also some marginal cases where seniors narrowly missed out on one criterion, but met the other criteria by a big margin.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For such appeals, we consider their circumstances in total and decide on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: However, the majority of the appeal cases are still pending because CPF Board is waiting for the appellants to provide additional information and documents for us to reassess their eligibility.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The Silver Support Scheme will cost close to $320 million in the first year to support about 140,000 of our seniors.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It complements the extensive range of support schemes for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Seniors who do not qualify for Silver Support but require financial assistance can approach any Social Service Office for help.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As the Minister for Finance said at Budget 2016, and I quote, "the majority of our seniors, even if they do not qualify for Silver Support, will continue to benefit from Page: 27 substantial existing support schemes".

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I have residents who said that their children are staying with them to help look after them because they are advanced in age and then because their children are staying with them, their household income has exceeded the requirement for the scheme.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The solution seems to be to ask the children to shift out and that seems to defeat the purpose of having children look after the elderly.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would the Ministry consider situations like these, where the children stay to look after their parents, but their income should not be included because they are doing it as a matter of filial piety?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Is CPF Board open to having, say, open houses at community centres to do better outreach to try to better explain to the seniors who do not really understand what this scheme is about?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many of my residents do tell me that they feel disadvantaged because their neighbours get it, and they do not.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The solution is not for the children or the senior to move out of the house; the solution is for the children to continue to take care of the senior.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The second point about the outreach, website and hotline, I agree with the Member.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Most of the seniors would come to CPF Service Centres.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the same time, we are also arranging a series of community outreach.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Many of the People's Association staff are equipped with the information.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I am also happy to say that quite a number of our grassroots advisers are also helping to bring the information out there to the community.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In any case, I hope that the children or the seniors do not move out of the house.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They should continue to live together and take care of each other.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We seem to suggest that children should only look after their parents if they live with the parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could the Minister clarify on this, please?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The point Mr Louis Ng is asking, if I get him right, is why is it that when we compute the per capita household income, we included only children who live with the seniors, and we do not include children who do not live with the seniors?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This means not so much using per capita household income but per capita family income as a criterion.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, we look at it as a family, whether the children are staying together or not and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I think, on the whole, no outcome is perfect.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, one of the key considerations of this scheme is that we would like to make the scheme as convenient for the seniors as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, under the Silver Support Scheme, the seniors need not apply for the scheme.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the per capita household income, we are able to gather the information through various sources, but that should not rule out, who knows, one day in the future, when we have enhanced our information network, we may one day evolve towards per capita family income basis.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But as of now, we do it on a per capita household income.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For cases if, indeed, the seniors feel that they deserve special consideration, help them to put up an appeal and, as I mentioned, we will look at the three criteria in totality.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If they do not qualify based on the per capita household income criterion, but if we take into consideration the other two criteria, if we feel that, on the whole, they deserve that extra help, we will extend the Silver Support to them.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: For those who qualify for Silver Support, the criteria, are they subject to review annually or are they set for life?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, come November this year, we will complete the review for 2017, and the seniors will receive a letter of notification from CPF in December this year and that will apply for 2017.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But any time during the year if any of the seniors feel that their family circumstances have changed, maybe the income has dropped or whatever, they can request for a review any time during the year and CPF Board will conduct a review.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those who turn out to be eligible, they will qualify for Silver Support from the date of appeal without having to wait for the annual cycle.
